category_title: Low-achieving students with disruptive behaviors and high absenteeism
minimal_context: The student is asked to classify 22 words written on the whiteboard and name each category during a classroom session.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Alright everyone, look at the 22 words on the whiteboard. I need you to stay in your assigned seats, classify these words into groups, and write down a name for each class.

STUDENT: (Stands up from desk) I don't want to sit here. I'm going over to that group to talk to my friends.

TUTOR: Please sit back down and focus on the words on the board.

STUDENT: Why can't we pick our own groups or play a game instead? We should be able to suggest activities we actually want to do.

TUTOR: We are not playing a game today. You need to stay quiet and do the classification task.

STUDENT: (Argues loudly) I'm not just going to sit here and be quiet! This is stupid, I'm leaving. (Walks out of the classroom door)

options.A: Ask the students to say the words out loud one by one, write them on the whiteboard, and have them discuss in self-selected groups to come up with their classifications.
options.B: Tell the student to take a few minutes to calm down outside the classroom door before returning to their assigned seat to complete the word classification task.
options.C: Use a brief, questioning intervention ('I'm sorry?') to signal that the student's language is inappropriate, and then acknowledge the student's apology ('Thank you') before returning to the whiteboard.
options.D: Provide a direct explanation of the meaning of the 22 words on the whiteboard, telling the student exactly how to classify them into groups for the classroom session.
